package_info.why_malicious: This report does not describe a specific malicious package or provide any code samples. Instead, it discusses general supply chain attack scenarios (e.g., event-stream, Webmin, Browserify typosquatting) and how SLSA and Sonatype products can help detect or prevent such attacks. No concrete package, version, or code is analyzed.

behavioral_signatures: Package versions that appear benign and later introduce malicious code
Packages whose source does not match the expected repository or provenance
Typosquatting: packages with names similar to popular packages but with malicious payloads
Packages that are uploaded to or served from untrusted or compromised mirrors
file_indicators: Unexpected or mismatched source files in package builds
Packages with provenance records that do not match the expected source control
Packages uploaded by unknown or suspicious accounts
network_indicators: Packages that attempt to contact external domains not associated with the project
Packages that are downloaded from non-official or untrusted mirrors
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages whose provenance does not match the expected source repository or builder. Flag packages that are typosquats of popular libraries or that have been recently updated with significant code changes. Use behavioral analysis to detect packages that attempt to exfiltrate data or contact suspicious domains. Employ repository firewalls and component intelligence to quarantine and review suspicious or untrusted packages before they enter the build pipeline.
